text: 192.168.100.2 sends 480,590 ICMP echo requests to 192.168.100.1 at a steady rate of about 7,600 per second, one every 130 microseconds.
source_text: 192.168.100.2 sent 480,590 ICMP echo requests (type 8, code 0) to 192.168.100.1, a steady rate of about 7,600 requests per second, one every 130 microseconds, with no pauses from the first packet to the last.

text: The echo requests carry no payload data and are minimum-size 60-byte frames, all with the same ICMP identifier and an incrementing sequence number.
source_text: The requests carry no payload data: each is a minimum-size 60-byte Ethernet frame. All of them use the same ICMP identifier, 0xcf6b, and the sequence number simply increments by one per packet, wrapping around as it overflows.

text: 192.168.100.1 answers every request with a 42-byte ICMP echo reply to 192.168.100.2 about 13 microseconds later.
source_text: 192.168.100.1 answered each request with an ICMP echo reply (type 0) of 42 bytes, about 13 microseconds after the request.

text: The echo requests and replies between the two hosts together reach about 6.2 Mbit/s for 63 seconds.
source_text: In total 480,590 replies were sent back to 192.168.100.2, one for every request, and the two directions together reached about 6.2 Mbit/s.
